comments.note: In prompt_renderer.py the _IF_BLOCK_RE pattern uses r'^\{\{#if\s+(\w+)\}\}' which only allows word chars (no hyphens) for the conditional variable name. This is inconsistent with the \w- pattern used for file names, though in practice all current template variables use underscores/words. Consider documenting this restriction explicitly.

The ValueError message interpolates the user-supplied name via f-string ({stage!r}). This is safe since it only goes to the exception message, but future logging middleware should be aware of this if it forwards exception messages to external systems.

comments.note: Python's \w in re.fullmatch matches Unicode word characters (e.g., 'naïve', CJK chars) by default, so such names pass the guard and then hit FileNotFoundError. Not a security issue (Unicode chars cannot form path separators). Worth noting in docs if the caller population ever widens beyond the pipeline stages.

Very long names (e.g., 500+ chars) pass the \w- guard and would hit an OS-level OSError when pathlib tries to open a file with a name exceeding OS limits. Low risk given this is an internal API used only by the orchestrator nodes.

comments.note: A01 — Path Traversal: load_template() and load_partial() both apply re.fullmatch(r'[\w-]+', name) before any filesystem operation. Paths are anchored to the package-relative templates/ directory. The _INCLUDE_RE regex captures (\w-]+ so include directives are constrained by the same rule. load_partial() re-validates the captured name (defense-in-depth). No path traversal vector exists.

A04 — Unicode \w pass-through (Info, previously noted by Developer and QA): Python re.fullmatch defaults to UNICODE, so names like 'naïve' or CJK characters pass validation. These cannot form path separators or traversal sequences; worst outcome is FileNotFoundError on an absent file. Not exploitable with the current internal caller set.

A04 — Very-long name OSError (Info, previously noted by QA): Names exceeding OS path limits pass the \w- guard and raise OSError at the pathlib.read_text() call rather than FileNotFoundError. Not exploitable for the current fixed set of pipeline stage names used as callers.

A09 — ValueError message interpolates user-supplied name via f-string ({stage!r}). Safe in exception context. Any future logging middleware forwarding exception messages to external sinks should sanitize this. Already flagged by Developer in implementation pipeline.

A03 — render_prompt uses str.format_map with defaultdict(str). Single-pass substitution: variable values containing {braces} are never doubly evaluated. Templates are loaded exclusively from controlled local files. No injection vector through variable substitution.
A06 — No new third-party dependencies introduced. Module uses only Python stdlib (re, pathlib, collections.defaultdict). No CVE exposure from this change.

summary: Reviewed 3 files: prompt_renderer.py, test_prompt_renderer.py, api-surface.md. PASS with one Fix-Forward applied.

Validation guards: re.fullmatch(r'[\w-]+', name) placed correctly before cache lookup in both load_template() and load_partial(). Guard fires before any filesystem access — invalid names never pollute the cache. Symmetric implementation across both functions with consistent error messages. Correct use of re.fullmatch (anchors both ends, no prefix-bypass possible).

[documentation-forward] _IF_BLOCK_RE uses (\w+) (no hyphens) while _INCLUDE_RE uses ([\w-]+). The distinction — conditional variable names vs. partial file names — is intentional but not documented. Add a brief inline comment in prompt_renderer.py explaining why _IF_BLOCK_RE excludes hyphens (template variable names are Python identifiers; partial file names follow kebab-case convention).

re.fullmatch defaults to UNICODE so Unicode word characters (e.g. 'naïve') pass the guard and reach FileNotFoundError. Confirmed non-exploitable by Security Auditor for the current fixed internal caller set. If the API is ever exposed beyond pipeline stage names, consider re.fullmatch(r'[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+', name) with re.ASCII to restrict to ASCII only.
